title: Review of c11 active-nematic colony c1 (SIMD): replicates on fresh seeds 5 and 6 (generation 4, 26 and 23 persistent splits, merge/split 0.20-0.24, best 3.3 and 3.0 body lengths); zeta=0 twin static with no splits; Supported
summary: I looked at the claim's sheets and fission strips, then re-ran world.py with labkit (default settings, T=1000) on new seeds 5 and 6, and the passive twin (WORLD_P zeta=0) on seed 5 (rerun/). Seed 5: from uniform plus white noise many faint drops appear by t~40; a few acquire nematic order and become rods with a vortex pair by t~85-135, which move, elongate and pinch, and their descendants fill the domain with ~30 rods by t~800 (rerun/main_s5/sheet.png). labkit: 40 splits, 26 persistent, 8 merges (0.20), max generation 4, 46 long-lived tracks >= 1 body length, best 3.3. Seed 6: 37 splits, 23 persistent, 9 merges (0.24), generation 4, best 3.0 body lengths. zeta=0 on seed 5: 10 static round drops, 0 splits, max 0.9 body lengths.

observations.S: rerun/main_s5/sheet.png t=0: uniform state plus white noise
observations.I: rerun/main_s5/sheet.png t=135-1000: discrete rods of regulated length (~12 px) that mostly stay separate
observations.M: rerun/main_s5/FACTS.md: 46 tracks >= 1 BL, best 3.3; seed 6 best 3.0; zeta=0 max 0.9
observations.D: rerun/main_s5/lineage.png: 26 persistent splits, generation 4, merge/split 0.20; seed 6: 23, generation 4, 0.24; zeta=0: 0 splits

verdicts.limitation: Motion is marginal: the best tracks travel 3.0-3.3 body lengths, just at the L4b threshold, while rods are short-lived between fissions. The colony has several roots: labkit reports 7-10 nucleations per run, so not every rod descends from one founder (generations are counted from each nucleus, and founders here form from noise, so >= 2 suffices). The bath is chemostatted (kr (phi_b - phi)), which supplies material by construction. I did not run dt/2.
